newsitem.title: UK: Siebe profits jump, confident of growth.
newsitem.headline: Siebe profits jump, confident of growth.

text.p: British engineering group Siebe Plc on Thursday reported a 28.1 percent jump in pretax profits to 424.1 million pounds ($693.9 million) for the year to April 5, 1997.
The controls systems group said in a statement it sees no signs of recession in any of its main markets and is "very confident of continuing the underlying growth in Siebe's business operations".
"Although currencies remain a concern, the group is able to manage the situation by flexing production volumes between countries," chairman Barrie Stephens said in the results statement.
The jump in pre-tax profits was achieved on the back of a 15.6 percent surge in sales to 3.01 billion pounds. The group announced a total dividend of 14.70 pence a share, up 10.4 percent.
The order backlog at the end of the year stood at 883.3 million pounds, up 23.4 percent on the year before. "This has given Siebe a very good start to the new year," Stephens said.

International sales amounted to 2.77 billion pounds, or 92.1 percent of total sales, of which 41.8 percent were in North America, 27.7 percent in continental Europe, 15.3 percent in the Pacific region and 7.3 percent the rest of the world. UK sales accounted for 7.9 percent of the total, or 237.7 million pounds.
"Overall, currency exchange had an unfavourable translational effect of 138.4 million pounds on sales and 16.8 million on profit before tax, which arose mainly in the second half," the company said.
